reasons: intent_insensitive: question four is no: a different enemy intent would not have changed the line, so the intent is not part of the decision

answers.q1_what_did_you_play: I played Mine Toss on Shrinker Beetle, then played Bag of Tricks and chose the option that spends 3 Sparks to place 3 Bombs dealing 5. This places a total of 4 Bombs on the enemy for 20 base bomb damage, spends the starting 3 Sparks, and then regains 1 Spark per Bomb detonation through Pounding Surprise.
answers.q2_other_line_considered: I seriously considered playing only Bag of Tricks with the 3-Spark option, which would place 3 Bombs for 15 damage and leave the Spark bank at 3 at the end of the turn. I also briefly considered adding a free block card such as Run Away!, but the enemy’s telegraphed action is only a Debuff, so block did not change the known outcome.
answers.q3_what_it_gave_up: The chosen line gave up the chance to keep the 3 Sparks unspent by taking the 1-Bomb option of Bag of Tricks, and it gave up the chance to gain Block this turn. It also left 2 Energy unused because the only damage card in hand is Mine Toss and the remaining cards are Block cards.
answers.q4_different_intent: No. A different enemy intent would not have changed the line as long as the enemy was not telegraphing an attack large enough to make Block necessary. If the enemy had telegraphed a high-damage attack, I would have considered spending the remaining Energy on Spirited Away or Duck and Cover, but the printed intent is Strategic/Debuff, so the damage-and-Spark line remains best.

survives_means: not yet falsified -- this funnel refuses turns and never rates them

targets.rule: a play that names a card whose effects aim at ONE enemy must carry that enemy's printed name in `target`; a card that aims at nobody must carry `target: null`
targets.derived_from: the card sheets (understudy/resource_order.SHEETS: the three character sheets, the three companion sheets and docs/prototype-surface.yaml), read through each effect's own `target:` key. The blind packet carries NO targeting field -- the wire's hand entry has none -- so the sheet is the derivation and this is the record of it
targets.repair: out of scope by M63: this refuses a form and never repairs one

closeness_quotability: the decision-closeness gap is a falsifier reading of the TURN and is quotable under R215 B's exception; it is never evidence that a decision is fun
guardrail: staged board: this hand and this board were set by hand through a dev door, so nothing measured here is comparable to any run, and nothing here is a claim about whether the turn is fun
